title: Search Index Lifecycle
readerIntent: Design and operate index creation, synchronization, evolution, reconciliation, and retirement.
priorKnowledge: Understand authoritative schemas and derived search indexes.
owner: Owning business capability, nSearch, and configured provider
summary: Indexes are derived projections whose mappings, documents, aliases, and lifecycle must remain reconcilable with authoritative records.

sections.heading: Lifecycle stages
items: Define index ownership, identity, fields, tenant routing, and refresh policy.
Create mapping and index or alias structures.
Populate initial records in bounded batches.
Apply incremental create, update, and delete changes.
Detect indexing lag, missing documents, duplicates, and mapping conflicts.
Reindex into a new version when incompatible mappings change.
Switch aliases only after validation.
Retire old indexes through a governed cleanup and rollback window.

sections.heading: Failure behavior
paragraphs: A successful database mutation and a failed index mutation must remain observable and reconcilable. Do not report the search projection as authoritative or silently discard partial bulk failures.

sections.heading: Schema evolution
items: Classify compatible versus incompatible field changes.
Version mappings and aliases when in-place updates are unsafe.
Test old and new query behavior before cutover.
Preserve tenant isolation and rollback evidence throughout migration.

sections.heading: Initial index build
paragraphs: Create the mapping from the effective search model, read authoritative records through governed services, and populate bounded batches. Record source position, counts, rejects, duration, and provider results.
Validate document count, samples, tenant routing, queries, permissions, and lag before exposing the new alias.

sections.heading: Incremental synchronization
items: Create and update after authoritative commit.
Remove or tombstone after lifecycle change.
Use stable identity and idempotent delivery.
Retry transient failure within bounds.
Record poison documents for governed repair.
Measure lag from authoritative change to searchable projection.

sections.heading: Reindex and alias cutover
items: Create a new versioned index and mapping.
Backfill from the authority while capturing concurrent changes.
Validate counts, samples, tenant isolation, and query acceptance.
Apply remaining changes and switch the alias atomically where supported.
Observe the new version and retain a rollback window.
Retire the old index only after approval.

sections.heading: Reconciliation
paragraphs: Compare authoritative identities, versions, and expected documents with the index. Repair missing, stale, duplicate, unauthorized, and orphaned projections without treating indexed content as truth.
Large reconciliation is rate-limited so it does not overwhelm persistence or search.

sections.heading: Verification matrix
items: Empty and populated initial build.
Create, update, delete, publish, and import synchronization.
Duplicate, out-of-order, and partial bulk delivery.
Mapping conflict and rejected document.
Provider outage, restart, resume, and reconciliation.
Alias cutover, rollback, cleanup, and tenant isolation.
